claims.text: Avenue Supermarts Limited (DMart) operates a national supermarket chain with a focus on value-retailing, offering a wide range of products in Foods, Non-Foods (FMCG), and General Merchandise & Apparel categories.

cites.quote: Avenue Supermarts Limited (DMart) is a national supermarket chain, with a focus on value-retailing. We offer a wide range of products with a focus on the Foods, Non-Foods (FMCG) and General Merchandise & Apparel product categories.

claims.text: DMart operates 500 stores across 15 states, 1 Union Territory, and NCR, with a retail business area of 20.58 million sq. ft.

cites.quote: DMart, our retail chain, was conceived by him in the year 2000. Mr. Damani imagined the retail business with the same values of simplicity, speed, and nimbleness that he espoused in his stellar investing career.

claims.text: DMart's strategy is based on the Everyday Low Cost/Everyday Low Price (EDLC/EDLP) principle, aiming to offer good quality products at great value.

cites.quote: We remain focussed on our strategy of offering our customers good quality products at great value, based on the Everyday Low Cost/Everyday Low Price (EDLC/EDLP) principle.

claims.text: DMart's revenue for FY26 was 68,821 crore, reflecting a growth of 15.9% from FY25.
The PAT for FY26 was 2,970 crore, with a PAT margin of 4.3%.
EBITDA margin for FY26 was 7.6%.
Revenue growth decelerated in Q3 FY26 by 2.2 percentage points compared to Q2 FY26.
Revenue growth accelerated in Q4 FY26 by 5.7 percentage points compared to Q3 FY26.
Revenue growth decelerated in Q1 FY27 by 4.1 percentage points compared to Q4 FY26.
Revenue growth accelerated in Q2 FY27 by 2.9 percentage points compared to Q1 FY27.
DMart's total borrowings for FY26 were 965 crore, with a debt/equity ratio of 0.04x.
The company's net worth stood at 24,462 crore.
DMart's CFO/PAT ratio improved from 91% in FY25 to 117% in FY26.
Free cash flow was negative in both FY25 and FY26, at -960 crore and -647 crore respectively.
In Q1 FY24, management expressed confidence in the online business, but no specific metrics were provided to measure this.
In Q1 FY25, management expressed confidence that the financial year would be equal to or better than FY24 GMA contribution, but this was not measurable from the results.
In Q1 FY26, management hoped to accelerate store openings, but the actual number of store openings was not disclosed in the results.
bull: DMart's revenue grew by 17.8% YoY in Q2 FY27, indicating strong sales performance.
bull: The company maintains a low debt/equity ratio of 0.04x, indicating financial stability.
bull: DMart's CFO/PAT ratio improved to 117% in FY26, reflecting strong cash generation relative to profit.
bear: DMart's PAT growth was only 8.5% YoY in Q2 FY27, lagging behind revenue growth.
bear: Free cash flow remained negative in FY26, indicating ongoing cash outflows exceeding cash inflows from operations.
bear: The company has not provided measurable guidance on store openings, limiting visibility into future expansion plans.

scorecard_takeaways.text: Management consistently expressed confidence in improving performance, but no specific measurable targets were set across the calls.
Revenue growth showed fluctuations, with periods of both acceleration and deceleration over the four quarters.
No numeric guidance items were measurable against delivered results, indicating a lack of specific targets or metrics.
